title: Enforce route-specific preflight and empty shutdown body
goal: The local Figma bridge accepts CORS preflight only for each route's exact method and headers, and POST /v1/shutdown cannot trigger shutdown unless its fully consumed request body is empty, including chunked transfer.

delivery.user_value: The local Figma bridge rejects misleading preflight permissions and body-bearing shutdown requests before the dependent plugin is integrated.

steps: Start a task-owned bridge with a stub manager and shutdown observer.
Replay the three wrong-route-method OPTIONS requests and unsupported route/header preflights; observe bounded rejection and no reflected permission.
Replay authenticated POST /v1/shutdown with a non-empty chunked body; observe rejection and confirm shutdown is not called, then verify a truly empty request succeeds.

work_classification.reason: This remediation tightens HTTP request validation only; it does not change Figma selection flow, plugin states, information architecture, or visible UI.

local.reason: The source bridge and its single remediation remain locally tracked with no external tracker, publication, deployment, or push.

reasons: Changes a security-sensitive local HTTP validation boundary, but only narrows accepted requests and is covered by exact transport reproducers and full bridge regression.

out: All bridge endpoints, response payloads, token/Host/origin rules, render request and PNG validation, capability/render semantics, runtime state, temporary-file lifecycle, process cleanup, and port binding except the two frozen request-validation blockers
server/mockup-mcp, dresser-preset/v1, .local/dresser-mirror, MANIFEST.sha256, Chrome/CDP automation, and existing MCP artifacts
figma-plugin manifest/controller/UI, visual gate, selection flow, canvas insertion, portfolio source, and generated dist assets
new dependencies, package.json or pnpm-lock.yaml changes, public transport, deployment, publication, Figma Community actions, Git push, force-push, merge, tag, or release
tasks/HISTORY.md, source-task evidence, unrelated task packets, and unrelated dirty-worktree changes

constraints: Implement one explicit preflight policy table for only /v1/capabilities, /v1/render, and /v1/shutdown; do not infer or echo the caller's requested method or headers as permission.

Allow /v1/capabilities preflight only for GET with authorization; allow /v1/render only for POST with authorization, content-type, and x-dresser-preset; allow /v1/shutdown only for POST with authorization. Header names and ordering may be case-insensitive, but required headers must be present and every extra header must be rejected.

For an allowed preflight, emit only the route's canonical Access-Control-Allow-Methods and Access-Control-Allow-Headers values. For an OPTIONS request to an unknown route, wrong route/method pair, missing required header, or extra header, return the existing bounded NOT_FOUND or INVALID_PREFLIGHT error without reflecting unsupported permissions or invoking manager/shutdown behavior.

POST /v1/shutdown must fully and boundedly consume the request stream before responding or scheduling shutdown, and must accept only zero decoded body bytes. Reject any decoded byte from Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding: chunked with the existing redacted INVALID_BODY contract; a valid zero-length request, including an empty chunked stream, may retain the existing 202 response.

Do not rely only on Content-Length, do not begin shutdown before end-of-stream validation, and preserve bounded handling of abort, stream error, conflicting framing rejected by Node, and slow/incomplete bodies without logging body bytes or token values.

Add automated regression cases for the exact four integration reproducers plus the valid per-route preflight matrix, unsupported OPTIONS route/header combinations, empty Content-Length shutdown, and empty versus non-empty chunked shutdown; assert no manager call or shutdown callback on every rejected request.

Preserve all passing source-task behavior and evidence boundaries, including loopback-only binding, Host/origin/token validation, capabilities, render, BUSY, error redaction, temporary cleanup, owned process cleanup, exact mirror integrity, MCP schemas, and interactive Dresser behavior.
Preserve unrelated dirty-worktree changes and do not edit package metadata, mirror/MCP/plugin/portfolio files, generated dist, source-task evidence, or perform external delivery.
acceptance_criteria: OPTIONS /v1/capabilities requesting POST, OPTIONS /v1/render requesting GET, and OPTIONS /v1/shutdown requesting GET each return a bounded rejection, expose no Access-Control-Allow-Methods or Access-Control-Allow-Headers permission for the requested combination, and call neither manager nor shutdown.

The valid route matrix is exact: capabilities permits only GET plus authorization, render permits only POST plus authorization/content-type/x-dresser-preset, and shutdown permits only POST plus authorization; response permission headers are canonical and are not derived by reflecting caller input.

OPTIONS to an unsupported route, a supported route missing any required preflight header, or a supported route requesting any extra header returns stable NOT_FOUND or INVALID_PREFLIGHT JSON with no unsupported CORS permission, manager call, shutdown callback, token disclosure, or stack trace.

Authenticated POST /v1/shutdown with any decoded body byte, including the verified non-empty chunked reproducer, returns the existing bounded INVALID_BODY error and does not send 202, schedule shutdown, remove runtime state, or close the listener.

Authenticated POST /v1/shutdown with a truly empty fully consumed body succeeds with the unchanged 202 response for both explicit Content-Length: 0 and an empty chunked stream, and invokes shutdown exactly once only after validation.

Automated tests reproduce all four reported failures before the fix, pass after it, and cover the complete allowed/denied route-method-header matrix plus empty/non-empty shutdown framing without weakening existing assertions.
The complete bridge suite, scoped lint/build, MCP suite, mirror integrity, and source-task neighbor behaviors pass with changes limited to the four frozen files.

checks.description: Replay the three wrong route/method OPTIONS requests and the authenticated non-empty chunked shutdown request from integration-blocker.md against a task-owned bridge; record stable rejection, absent permission reflection, listener/runtime continuity, and zero manager/shutdown calls.

Exercise every valid route/method/header combination, every cross-route method, missing required header, extra header, case/order variant, and unknown OPTIONS route; verify only canonical allowed responses and bounded NOT_FOUND or INVALID_PREFLIGHT negatives.

Exercise Content-Length 0, positive length, absent length, empty chunked, non-empty chunked, slow/incomplete, aborted, and parser-rejected conflicting framing; require full empty-body validation before the sole successful shutdown callback and liveness after every app-level rejection.

Inspect the four-file scoped diff and rerun passing auth, Host, origin, capability, render, BUSY, redaction, cleanup, MCP, and mirror checks; confirm no package, runtime-state, UI, portfolio, mirror, MCP contract, task-history, or unrelated dirty-worktree change.

steps: Revert only TASK-DRESSER-FIGMA-001-R1 changes in server.mjs, protocol.mjs, server.test.mjs, and protocol.test.mjs.
Stop only any R1 test-owned bridge listener, remove only its disposable runtime/input state, and rerun the source bridge tests, lint, build, MCP tests, and mirror-integrity command.

history.summary: Reject cross-route CORS preflights and body-bearing shutdown requests before any bridge side effect.
